artifacts.summary: 6-phase plan: build and register a standing script-inventory probe (Phases 1-3), then three bounded behaviour-preserving lib/ extractions from orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (Phases 4-6).

memory_candidates.content: Sizing bash functions by the line-delta between consecutive top-level `name() {` definitions is unreliable, not merely imprecise. In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh the proxy over-reported individual functions by up to 31x (build_contended_manifest: 657 claimed vs 100 actual; task_has_forced_phase: 358 vs 9), because the file is one 2,264-line monolithic function (orchestrate_cycle_plan_main, 74.8% of the file) containing 13 helper functions defined at COLUMN 0 inside its body. Column-0 `}` therefore does not delimit a top-level function, and the lines between two definitions are the enclosing function's straight-line body, not the earlier function's extent. Correct method: track brace depth across the file and pair each opening definition with the close at its own depth. The structural consequence matters for refactoring, not just measurement: helpers are nested precisely because they close over the enclosing function's locals, so extracting one into scripts/lib/ requires converting every implicit closure into an explicit parameter (and serializing bash associative arrays as JSON) rather than moving text.
